scope_decision.chosen: (c) marked umbrella spans in upstream + hash-pinned orchestra alternates in a sidecar + a fail-closed leak gate + one path token
mechanism: PATHS are tokenized, CONCEPTS are marked. Every literal 'graph_agents' in a payload file becomes the single token '@FLEET@' (fleet root, rendered by Orchestra at install time). No other path rewriting.

CONCEPT spans (umbrella invariant, registry-first routing, repos/ launch rule, TelosRG, CURRENT-STATE/HISTORY, conventions/ and decisions/ pointers, references to excluded skills/hooks, dated incidents that name the umbrella) are wrapped upstream in whole-line markers: '<!-- umbrella:begin <id> -->' / '<!-- umbrella:end <id> -->' in Markdown prose, '# umbrella:begin <id>' / '# umbrella:end <id>' in Python, YAML frontmatter and fenced bash. No nesting, no mid-line spans.

Alternates live OUTSIDE the agent files, in graph_agents/.graph/orchestra-sync/alternates/{prose.md,code.md,json.json}, keyed by marker id. Each entry carries a pin: sha256 (12 hex) of the umbrella span it replaces. Empty body = drop. Sync REFUSES on: marker without entry, entry without marker (orphan), or pin mismatch (umbrella span was tuned since the alternate was written; tool prints the new hash, a human re-reads and re-pins).

JSON files cannot carry markers, so settings.json and runs/_schema.json are handled by pinned JSON-pointer patches in alternates/json.json (remove/replace, each pinned to the old value) - same drift guard.

LEAK GATE, fail closed: after render, every payload file is scanned against a denylist (repos/, registry.json, portfolio, TelosRG/telosrg, lowercase 'umbrella'/'Umbrella', CURRENT-STATE, HISTORY.md, audit-fleet, verify-invariant, flag-cross-app-import, flag-stale-state, guard-commit-trailers, new-app, fleetview, postmortem, conventions/, decisions/, njcurtis3, absolute user paths, AND every app id read live from portfolio/registry.json). Any hit not in payload.json leak_allow (file + pattern + reason) refuses the sync. Registry absent -> refuse (the denylist would be silently weaker). The 'UMBRELLA' Python constant is case-distinct and not a hit.

UMBRELLA RENDER IDENTITY: '--verify-upstream <commit>' renders each payload file in umbrella mode (marker lines deleted, spans kept, no tokens) and byte-compares to 'git show <commit>:<file>'. This proves marking changed nothing the umbrella agents/hooks execute or read, except the marker lines themselves.

Strip-only without alternates leaves steps dangling (scout step 1 reads the registry; drop it and scout has no first step). (c) keeps (a)'s single source of truth and moves only the alternates out.
scope_decision.why_not_b: (b) whole-file overlays: the drift is the whole problem. Every tune to architect.md upstream would silently not reach Orchestra's overlay copy, which defeats the stated goal (tune in graph_agents, carry tunes to Orchestra). Nothing mechanical would notice.

A standing maintenance tax: any future upstream edit that introduces an umbrella concept outside a marker makes the next sync refuse until it is marked. That is the intended failure mode (loud), but it is a tax on every tuning session that touches payload files.
Re-pinning is a human step whenever a marked span is tuned. Drift is detected, not prevented: a re-pin without re-reading the alternate is possible and nothing can catch it.
The leak gate proves absence of listed strings, not absence of umbrella meaning. Concept leaks phrased without a denylisted word pass. That is why every slice that writes alternates is risk high.

design_notes: INSTALL LAYOUT this payload assumes (stated so Orchestra's later run inherits it, not decided for it): Orchestra copies fleet/ into an end-user project as ONE directory segment under the project root, <project>/<fleet-dir>/, and renders '@FLEET@' -> <fleet-dir>. Under that layout every existing __file__-relative constant is already correct: FLEET = the installed dir, UMBRELLA = dirname(FLEET) = the project root (so guard-builder-scope.py:439-441's fallback base is the right base), settings.json commands resolve via CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/<fleet-dir>/.claude/hooks/, and run state (.graph/CURRENT, runs/, worktrees/) is written into the INSTALLED copy, never into orchestra/fleet/. This dissolves the scout's 'run state inside the vendored tree' risk: orchestra/fleet/ is a template, not a runtime directory.

REFUSAL RULE, interpreted: the SOURCE manifest is the authority. Sync refuses iff any file under the target (other than README.md, which is orchestra-owned and never written) is missing from SOURCE.files, has a different hash, or a SOURCE-listed file is missing. Uncommitted changes that MATCH SOURCE are the sync's own pending output and are allowed, which is what makes a re-run idempotent before the owner commits. First sync: allowed only when the target holds nothing but README.md and no SOURCE. Hashes are computed on LF-normalized bytes so git autocrlf on another machine is not mistaken for a hand-edit.

UPSTREAM CLEANLINESS: sync refuses if git -C graph_agents status --porcelain shows changes in any payload path or in .graph/orchestra-sync/ (the run's own untracked .graph/runs/<id>/ does not count). SOURCE names a commit, and a dirty tree would make that a lie.

SOURCE format (JSON, no extension, no wall-clock timestamp so a re-run is byte-identical): upstream_repo 'graph_agents', upstream_commit (full sha), upstream_commit_date, sync_tool_version, token {'@FLEET@': 'fleet root, render at install'}, files {path: sha256}, dropped_hooks [names], unmanaged ['README.md'].

SELF-CONSISTENCY CHECKS (all fail closed, all exercised by fixture tests): (1) every settings.json hook command resolves to a payload file, checked with '|| true' stripped; (2) every payload .py's sibling loads - 'import <name>' where <name>.py exists upstream beside it, and spec_from_file_location / join(HERE, '<x>.py') literals - resolve inside the payload; (3) every backticked .claude/... / .graph/... / @FLEET@/... path in payload prose resolves inside the payload; (4) every payload .py passes py_compile; (5) smoke: render into <tmp>/proj/fleet with '@FLEET@' -> 'fleet', git init proj, run each settings hook command with stdin '{}' and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=proj, each exits 0 without its '|| true'.

s1.$comment: RE-REVIEWS NEST, and this is the rule every reader follows. The TOP LEVEL of reviews.<slice> IS attempt 1. A re-review writes attempt_2, then attempt_3, and so on, each with the same fields as the top level. Every attempt SURVIVES PERMANENTLY - history is never overwritten, flattened, or migrated up. The LATEST attempt supplies the verdict: that is what close-run.py, brief.py and verify-state.py resolve through, and what fleetview's finalVerdict() has always shown. `ever_rejected` - did ANY attempt REJECT - is DISPLAY ONLY, forever, so a rejection stays visible after it is fixed; it must never gate anything, or the fleet stops being able to loop. NO NODE MAY REWRITE AN EARLIER ATTEMPT: a second reviewer writes its own attempt_N and leaves the ones before it alone, top-level verdict included - relocating that verdict would destroy the history the board keeps and leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author. The KEY INDEX numbers an attempt, not the `attempt` field inside it; the field is display. An EMPTY attempt_N is not a re-review, it is a key nobody wrote - write the whole attempt or none of it. The walk STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP, so an attempt_3 with no attempt_2 is ignored and the earlier verdict stands: A GAP IS MALFORMED AND NO NODE MAY LEAVE ONE. Write the next UNUSED N and never skip - a mis-numbered re-review is not reported anywhere, it is simply unread, and a REJECT nobody reads is a REJECT nobody acts on. The cap is attempt_9, matching fleetview's `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` exactly so the two readers cannot disagree; attempt_10 and beyond is reported loudly and resolved by nobody.
